question: What happens when the INTENSITY (brightness) of incident light is increased while keeping its frequency constant (with f > f0)?
correct_answer: The number of photoelectrons emitted per second increases (photocurrent increases), but the maximum kinetic energy (Ek(max)) and maximum velocity of the photoelectrons remain completely unchanged.
wrong_answers_pool: The maximum kinetic energy (Ek(max)) of the photoelectrons increases proportionally.
The work function of the metal decreases.
Both the photocurrent and the kinetic energy of the electrons increase.
The speed of the emitted photoelectrons increases.
The threshold frequency of the metal shifts to a lower value.
Electrons stop being emitted because the metal overheats.

tags.subject: Physical Sciences
tags.topic: Paper 1: Optical Phenomena and Properties of Matter
tags.learning_outcome: Explain effects of frequency and intensity

question: What happens when the FREQUENCY of incident light is increased while keeping its intensity constant (with f > f0)?
correct_answer: The maximum kinetic energy (Ek(max)) and maximum speed (v_max) of the emitted photoelectrons increase, while the number of photoelectrons emitted per second remains constant.
wrong_answers_pool: The number of photoelectrons emitted per second increases dramatically.
The work function of the metal increases.
The photocurrent increases proportionally with frequency.
The threshold frequency increases to match the new light frequency.
Both the kinetic energy and the number of photoelectrons double.
The speed of the photoelectrons decreases as frequency increases.

tags.subject: Physical Sciences
tags.topic: Paper 1: Optical Phenomena and Properties of Matter
tags.learning_outcome: Explain effects of frequency and intensity

question: Monochromatic light of frequency f < f0 is shone onto a metal surface with very high intensity for two hours. What is observed?
correct_answer: Zero photoelectrons are emitted (No electrons are emitted, regardless of intensity or duration of illumination, because each individual photon lacks sufficient energy to overcome the work function W0).
wrong_answers_pool: Electrons are emitted after an accumulation delay of approximately ten minutes.
Electrons are emitted with very low kinetic energy.
Electrons are emitted in massive numbers because intensity is high.
The metal melts and emits protons.
Photoelectrons are emitted only from the surface layer.
The threshold frequency drops until emission begins.
